Rule Why Ingress from the namespace, from host and remote-node; egress to the namespace The rules every policy carries: What every policy contains Ingress on 8123 from the Authentik server pods only The outpost is the only path to the UI. No fromEntities: ingress, so a request straight from the Gateway cannot skip it. Nothing else in the cluster has a reason to connect: this namespace holds a long-lived token for every device in the house. With the rule missing, the hostname answers with a gateway error after a successful Authentik login Ingress from Prometheus on 9187, GET /metrics only The database's metrics; a week of Hubble records showed no other request Ingress from cnpg-system on 8000 The operator polls the instance manager there; without the rule the Cluster never goes Healthy and the sync deadlocks. See Sync stuck on the database Egress to *.home-assistant.io The alerts feed and version data. An integration that talks to a device or a cloud is a line here first Egress to the multicast and limited-broadcast ranges on 5353 and 1900 The mDNS and SSDP discovery sockets keep sending, and the overlay carries it nowhere. Allowed only so it does not fill the drop log Egress from the database pod to kube-apiserver The instance manager reports its status there; its liveness check fails otherwise. The object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's cnpg-backups policy, see CloudNativePG → Backups

items.title: Usage
items.text:
The ConfigMap is mounted over /config/configuration.yaml, so Git is the source of truth and the UI cannot edit it; everything Home Assistant writes for itself stays on the PVC underneath. The file is read once at startup, so a merged change does nothing until the pod restarts:

kubectl -n home-assistant rollout restart deploy/home-assistant

The UI's own restart button does the same from inside.

items.title: Health check
items.text:
kubectl -n home-assistant get pods,pvc
kubectl -n home-assistant get cluster home-assistant-db

The database should report Cluster in healthy state. A pod stuck in Init is waiting on it: the init container cannot write secrets.yaml until CloudNativePG has produced the Secret.

items.title: Pitfalls
items.text:
The API is not behind Authentik

/api/, /auth/token and the external-auth callback are exempt on the provider, so Home Assistant's own accounts guard them and revoking an Authentik account does not revoke a Home Assistant token: do that under Settings → People. See Authentik → Pitfalls.

  • No local device discovery. mDNS and SSDP need host networking, which needs a privileged namespace. Add devices by IP, or through an integration that does not rely on broadcast, and add the address to the egress policy.
  • No USB devices. A Zigbee or Z-Wave stick pins the pod to one machine. Use a network-attached coordinator instead.
  • The cluster is now a dependency of the lights. A Ceph rebalance that pauses I/O pauses Home Assistant with it.

items.title: Knead Time
items.text: Knead Time is a static pizza-dough calculator on GitHub Pages. Its step reminders cannot come from the page — iOS wakes a web app's service worker only for a server-sent push — so this is the one server it has: a small FastAPI service that holds a phone's push subscription and the times of its hands-on steps, and sends a Web Push notification when each comes due. The source and the image live in the knead-time repository, so like Flowscape it deploys as plain manifests around our own image, per Conventions → Official upstream sources only.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: URL kneadtime.k8s.wlkr.ch, an API under /v1; the app that calls it is kneadtime.pizza Authentication None. Browsers on kneadtime.pizza call it directly; CORS admits that origin only Storage None on the pod Database CloudNativePG Cluster kneadtime-db Dials The browsers' push services, over HTTPS Files kneadtime/

items.title: State
items.text: State Where Rebuildable? Push subscriptions and the reminders queued for them PostgreSQL, via CloudNativePG Only by every phone tapping Remind me again; a lost database means one missed bake, not a lost account The VAPID private key OpenBao kv/kneadtime/config, through an ExternalSecret No — rotating it retires every subscription taken with the old key

items.title: Configuration
items.text: Setting Why Plain manifests, no chart One process, one port, one database; the service README lists the environment and that is all there is The namespace enforces restricted The image runs as uid 65532, writes nothing and needs no capability; CloudNativePG's pods declare restricted-compliant contexts of their own One replica, the default RollingUpdate The dispatcher that sends due reminders runs inside the process and claims due rows with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so the two copies that overlap during a rollout never send the same reminder; nothing on the pod needs a Recreate gap A Cluster, not SQLite on a PVC Conventions → PostgreSQL is always a CloudNativePG Cluster; DATABASE_URL is the uri key the operator writes to kneadtime-db-app VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY from OpenBao A P-256 key in PEM, generated by make bao-secrets because a Password generator cannot produce one, which is why rule 7's PushSecret path does not apply; the service derives the public half at startup and serves it, so the static site carries no key VAPID_SUBJECT is the site URL The contact a push service may use; a URL rather than a mailbox keeps an address out of a manifest ALLOWED_ORIGINS is the site Only pages loaded from kneadtime.pizza may call the API from a browser; PR previews of the app live under the same origin FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS is the pod CIDR Envoy is the only thing that reaches the pod, and it appends the client's address to X-Forwarded-For; uvicorn trusts that header from the pod network only, so the service's per-address rate limit (ratelimit.py) counts the phone, not the Gateway HTTPRoute targets the app's own Service Nobody logs in — browsers call the API on behalf of a phone that already gave its subscription. The Dependency-Track shape, not the Flowscape one HTTPRoute matches /v1 only The app serves its API, its probes and /metrics on one port; the browser calls only /v1/vapid and /v1/schedules (src/lib/push/api.ts in the app repository), and the counters describe usage that is nobody else's business revisionHistoryLimit: 2 Superseded ReplicaSets keep their Trivy config-audit reports until garbage collection; the default keeps ten

items.title: Network policy
items.text:
The rules in kneadtime/networkpolicy.yaml, and why each is there. The shape is Conventions → Ship a CiliumNetworkPolicy.

Rule Why Ingress from the namespace, from host and remote-node; egress to the namespace The rules every policy carries: What every policy contains Ingress on 8080 from ingress The Gateway reaches the pod directly; there is no outpost to skip Ingress from Prometheus on 8080 and 9187, GET /metrics only The app's counters and the database's exporter Ingress from cnpg-system on 8000 The operator reads the instance manager's status Egress to the four push-service names on 443 Apple, Google, Mozilla and Microsoft are where subscriptions live. The service refuses any other host at request time, so this list and the code's allow-list are one decision taken twice The instance pods reach kube-apiserver The CloudNativePG instance manager reports its status there. The object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's cnpg-backups policy, see CloudNativePG → Backups

items.title: Secrets
items.text: kv/kneadtime/config holds one key, vapid-private-key, written by make bao-secrets in the platform repository. Overwriting it is gated behind a typed confirmation there: the push services answer 401 or 403 for every subscription taken with the old key, the service deletes them, and every phone has to opt in again.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
Nothing to operate by hand. A phone with the app on its Home Screen taps Remind me on this device in the plan's menu; the receipt notification that arrives at once is the end-to-end check.

curl -s https://kneadtime.k8s.wlkr.ch/v1/vapid     # the public key, from outside the LAN

items.title: Health check
items.text:
kubectl -n kneadtime get pods,cluster,externalsecret,httproute
kubectl -n kneadtime port-forward svc/kneadtime 8080:80 &
curl -s localhost:8080/metrics | grep kneadtime_push

kneadtime_push_sent_total moves when a reminder goes out; gone_total counts subscriptions the push services refused.

items.title: Pitfalls
items.text:
• The image has to be public on GHCR. The cluster has no pull secret for ghcr.io/janwelker; a version published while the package was private stays ImagePullBackOff until the package's visibility is changed.
  • readyz is the database. A pod that is up but not ready is a database that is not reachable; check the Cluster before the pod.
  • Nothing here sends on its own schedule. A reminder that did not arrive is either a subscription the push service retired (gone_total rose, the phone has to opt in again) or a phone whose Home Screen icon was removed, which drops the subscription on the device side.

items.title: OpenCloud
items.text: OpenCloud is the household's file sync and share: one Go binary, no database, with desktop, iOS and Android clients. Upstream publishes no open Helm chart, so opencloud/ is plain manifests around the official image: deployment.yaml, service.yaml, pvc.yaml, httproute.yaml, servicemonitor.yaml, secrets.yaml, networkpolicy.yaml, namespace.yaml and two ConfigMaps, csp.yaml and authentik-blueprint.yaml, per Conventions → Official upstream sources only.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: URL cloud.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch, LAN and VPN only Authentication Authentik OIDC for every client; the built-in identity provider does not run Storage rook-ceph-block PVC for /var/lib/opencloud, the PosixFS driver Database None; metadata lives in extended attributes and the embedded NATS store Secrets kv/opencloud/config in OpenBao, generated once Files opencloud/

items.title: Storage
items.text:
PosixFS keeps the files on the volume in the tree the user sees, with the metadata in xattrs, which ext4 provides, and versions, trash and the search index beside them. One volume holds the whole instance, so the nightly Velero snapshot is a complete copy, and a restore is readable with ls. The driver's non-collaborative mode requires that nothing else writes to the tree, which a single Deployment on a ReadWriteOnce volume guarantees.

The alternative, blobs in an S3 bucket with metadata on a volume, splits one instance across two backup mechanisms, one of which does not exist for buckets here, and upstream documents no migration into or out of it.

Upstream's backup guidance is to stop the instance first. The RBD snapshot is crash-consistent instead: metadata is written per operation on the same filesystem, and the nightly Velero run sees no sync traffic. The search index is rebuilt if it disagrees after a restore; nothing is lost.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
The values in opencloud/deployment.yaml that are not self-explanatory:

Setting Why opencloudeu/opencloud-rolling, not the production opencloudeu/opencloud Rolling ships every three weeks on a current Alpine; the production line gets a release about every six months, and its image carried a fixable critical in an Alpine package that the image-scan gate refuses. Move to the production line at a release that passes the gate. Either way a major bump waits for a human args: ["server"], no init opencloud init only writes random secrets and IDs into opencloud.yaml. Every one of them arrives as an environment variable from opencloud-env instead, so /etc/opencloud is an emptyDir and the pod carries nothing a backup would have to protect strategy: Recreate, one replica The volume is ReadWriteOnce, and PosixFS in non-collaborative mode tolerates one writer runAsUser: 1000, fsGroup: 1000, read-only root, the namespace enforces restricted The image runs as that user and writes only under /var/lib/opencloud, /etc/opencloud and /tmp, the last two emptyDirs OC_EXCLUDE_RUN_SERVICES=idp Authentik is the identity provider; the built-in one would be a second login OC_OIDC_ISSUER=https://auth.k8s.wlkr.ch/ The four Authentik providers run in global issuer mode, whose issuer is the bare hostname; see OIDC PROXY_CSP_CONFIG_FILE_LOCATION, the policy in opencloud/csp.yaml The default Content-Security-Policy allows connections and frames to the server itself only, so the browser refuses the discovery, token and silent-renew requests to an external IdP and the page spins forever. The file adds auth.k8s.wlkr.ch to connect-src and frame-src; OpenCloud merges it into the default rather than replacing it, so the default's update.opencloud.eu and GitHub app-store hosts stay in the browser policy. They matter only to a browser, the update check is off, and the server itself reaches neither PROXY_OIDC_REWRITE_WELLKNOWN The desktop and mobile clients discover the identity provider through the server's own /.well-known/openid-configuration PROXY_OIDC_ACCESS_TOKEN_VERIFY_METHOD=jwt Authentik's access tokens are JWTs, so the server checks signature and issuer itself instead of calling userinfo on every request PROXY_OIDC_AUDIENCES, the four client IDs Authentik writes the client ID into aud, so the server accepts only tokens minted for one of its own clients, not any token from the same issuer. Without the list the proxy logs at every start that audience validation is off PROXY_AUTOPROVISION_ACCOUNTS, with sub as the username Accounts are created in the built-in IDM on first login and keyed on the sub claim, which never changes, per Conventions → Authentication. Upstream's own autoprovisioning example does the same. Users see display names, never this value GRAPH_USERNAME_MATCH=none Authentik's sub is a SHA-256 hex string, and the default rule refuses a username that starts with a digit: Invalid username, and the first login ends in a 400 FRONTEND_READONLY_USER_ATTRIBUTES Name and mail come from Authentik on every login, so the profile page must not offer to edit them PROXY_ROLE_ASSIGNMENT_DRIVER=oidc on the groups claim, GRAPH_ASSIGN_DEFAULT_USER_ROLE=false The role comes from Authentik group membership, and a user in neither group gets no role and no access; see Usage STORAGE_USERS_ID_CACHE_STORE=nats-js-kv PosixFS requires the NATS key-value store for its id cache; the embedded NATS provides it FRONTEND_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES=false The web frontend's version check is the one outbound call the server makes on its own. Nothing phones home, the same rule as every platform component PROXY_DEBUG_ADDR=0.0.0.0:9205 Every service in the binary has a debug port; the proxy's carries the request metrics, the health endpoints and the one ServiceMonitor HTTPRoute on infra-gateway, not apps-gateway Only apps-gateway gets a public DNS record. Phones sync on the LAN and the VPN; moving to the public gateway is one route change

items.title: OIDC
items.text:
OpenCloud's web, desktop, iOS and Android clients are four OIDC clients with IDs fixed by the clients (web, OpenCloudDesktop, OpenCloudIOS, OpenCloudAndroid), all public, authorization code with PKCE, so opencloud/authentik-blueprint.yaml holds four providers and four applications. Only the web one is visible in the Authentik library; the native ones carry blank://blank as their launch URL.

The server and the native clients verify every token against the one issuer the server advertises, and Authentik derives a provider's issuer from its application slug. All four providers therefore use issuer_mode: global, and the platform rewrites /.well-known/openid-configuration on auth.k8s.wlkr.ch to the opencloud application's document; see One issuer for OpenCloud.

The desktop client redirects to a loopback address with a random port, so its redirect URI is a regular expression; the mobile ones are custom-scheme URLs the apps register. There are no client secrets, so nothing lands in OpenBao for Authentik's side, and the platform repository only mounts the blueprint.

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
secrets.yaml generates what opencloud init would: a Password generator for the JWT, transfer, URL-signing and service-account secrets, the machine-auth and system-user API keys and the IDM service passwords, which the users, groups, auth-basic and graph services also receive as their LDAP bind passwords, and one UUID generator per ID, because a UUID generator yields one value and a PushSecret reads one generator. Each PushSecret writes its keys into kv/opencloud/config once; the ExternalSecret templates them into opencloud-env under the environment variable names. Losing the OpenBao path and regenerating is a new instance: the JWT secret signs the internal tokens and the IDs name the storage mount and the system user, so the data on the volume would no longer match.

idm-admin-password is the built-in IDM's admin account, which the first start creates. With the IdP excluded nothing presents a login form for it, so there is no local break-glass account here, not even the one rule 6 allows: Authentik is the only way in.

items.title: Network policy
items.text:
The rules in opencloud/networkpolicy.yaml, and why each is there. The shape is Conventions → Ship a CiliumNetworkPolicy.

Rule Why Ingress from the namespace, from host and remote-node; egress to the namespace The rules every policy carries: What every policy contains Ingress from ingress on 9200 The Gateway reaches the server directly; OpenCloud handles its own login, and the desktop and mobile clients arrive the same way Ingress from Prometheus on 9205, GET /metrics only The proxy's metrics; the health endpoints on the same port are the kubelet's, covered by host and remote-node Egress from the server to the Authentik server pods on 9000 Discovery, the signing keys and the token endpoint go to auth.k8s.wlkr.ch, which resolves to the Gateway's own address, private but world to Cilium. The Gateway's Envoy then checks this policy against the Authentik pod it picks and answers 403 itself when that pod is not listed, so both the name and the pod are allowed Egress from the server to auth.k8s.wlkr.ch on 443 The other half of the same path. Hubble records one dropped SYN to this name at each pod start: the first packet after a fresh DNS answer races the FQDN policy update and the retransmit passes, the known artefact, not a missing rule

No app store, no update check, no mail, no object store: the search index and NATS run inside the process.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
Membership in one of two Authentik groups is an account:

Group OpenCloud role opencloudAdmin Administrator opencloudUser User

A user in neither group can log in to Authentik but is refused by OpenCloud with no role assigned. The groups also appear as groups inside OpenCloud, because autoprovisioning mirrors the groups claim.

Clients: the desktop client for macOS 13 and later, Windows and Linux, the iOS app from the App Store and the Android app from Google Play or F-Droid. Each takes the server URL and opens Authentik in the browser.

items.title: Health check
items.text:
kubectl -n opencloud get pods,pvc,externalsecret,pushsecret
curl -s https://cloud.infra.k8s.wlkr.ch/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq -r .issuer

The pod is Running, every PushSecret and the ExternalSecret are Ready, and the issuer printed is https://auth.k8s.wlkr.ch/. After a first start, the idm.boltdb on the volume is larger than the 32 KiB of an empty Bolt file; see Pitfalls.

kubectl -n opencloud exec deploy/opencloud -- ls -l /var/lib/opencloud/idm/

items.title: Pitfalls
items.text: Symptom Cause ExternalSecret stays SecretSyncedError on the first sync The PushSecrets and the ExternalSecret are in different waves but OpenBao is written asynchronously; the retry covers it within minutes The web page shows the loading animation forever, the console reports a Content-Security-Policy violation for auth.k8s.wlkr.ch The served policy is the default, not csp.yaml: the ConfigMap or PROXY_CSP_CONFIG_FILE_LOCATION is missing, or the mount path differs from the variable Login succeeds in Authentik, OpenCloud answers 403 The user is in neither group, or the issuer in the token differs from OC_OIDC_ISSUER: a provider without issuer_mode: global The desktop client's login tab never returns The loopback redirect did not match the regular expression; the port is random and the path may be empty Prometheus shows the target down The policy allows GET /metrics only; any other path on 9205 from Prometheus is refused Login ends on "Not logged in"; the log shows failed to add user with LDAP Result Code 49 from graph and not found from idm The IDM database under idm/ on the volume is a bare Bolt file: a first pod that died during the bootstrap, as in the row below, left it created but without the service users, and every later start sees the file and skips the bootstrap. Remove the idm directory (Recovery); the next start bootstraps it. Only safe while no account exists yet, which is the case when this symptom appears The pod exits with error parsing mapping JSON: unexpected end of JSON input from the search service The Bleve index under search/ on the volume was created by a pod that died before writing the mapping, which happens when another service fails on the same first start. Remove the search directory (Recovery); the index is rebuilt from the files on the next start

items.title: Removing a directory from the volume
items.text:
For the two first-start failures above. The volume is ReadWriteOnce and stays attached to the node of the crashing pod, so the debug pod goes on that node; scaling the Deployment to zero first does not hold, self-heal restores the replica within a minute.

  1. Start a debug pod beside the crashing one, on its node and from its image, with the restricted context the namespace enforces:

    NODE=$(kubectl -n opencloud get pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=opencloud -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.nodeName}')
IMAGE=$(kubectl -n opencloud get deploy opencloud -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')
kubectl -n opencloud apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: opencloud-debug
spec:
  nodeName: $NODE
  restartPolicy: Never
  automountServiceAccountToken: false
  securityContext:
    runAsNonRoot: true
    runAsUser: 1000
    runAsGroup: 1000
    fsGroup: 1000
    seccompProfile:
      type: RuntimeDefault
  containers:
    - name: shell
      image: $IMAGE
      command: ["sleep", "3600"]
      securityContext:
        allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
        capabilities:
          drop: ["ALL"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /var/lib/opencloud
  volumes:
    - name: data
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: opencloud-data
EOF

  2. Remove the directory, idm or search:

    kubectl -n opencloud exec opencloud-debug -- rm -r /var/lib/opencloud/search

  3. Delete the debug pod; the container's next restart recreates what was removed:

    kubectl -n opencloud delete pod opencloud-debug

items.title: Shot Timer bridge
items.text: The bridge is the always-on half of the Shot Timer iPhone app. iOS will not let an app hold the La Marzocco cloud websocket open in the background, so this one process watches the machine, tracks each shot, looks up the machine's exact extraction time afterwards, keeps the shot history in SQLite, and starts and updates the phone's Live Activity through APNs. The phone and watch apps call its small HTTP API. The source, the image and the chart live in somuch-cloud/extractor.cafe; the chart is published to ghcr.io/somuch-cloud/charts, per Conventions → Official upstream sources only.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: URL shot.k8s.wlkr.ch, an API for the iPhone and watch apps Authentication The bridge's own bearer key; the apps cannot go through Authentik Storage PVC shot-bridge, SQLite and the La Marzocco installation key Database CloudNativePG Cluster shot-bridge-db, a primary and a streaming replica Dials lion.lamarzocco.io, APNs Files shot-bridge/

items.title: State
items.text: State Where Rebuildable? Shot history, registered phones, default dose, coffees, reference shots PostgreSQL, the CloudNativePG Cluster shot-bridge-db (database.yaml) History from its WAL archive, to any point inside its retention window; phones re-register on their next launch La Marzocco installation key installation_key.json on the PVC Yes, the bridge registers a new one on start Account credentials and the APNs key OpenBao kv/shot-bridge/accounts Re-typed from the accounts API key OpenBao kv/shot-bridge/config, generated Yes, then entered again in the iPhone app

items.title: Configuration
items.text: Setting Why Own chart, values in application.yaml The chart ships the Deployment, PVC, Service, HTTPRoute and the bridge's CiliumNetworkPolicy; this directory adds the namespace, the secrets and the namespace's default-deny policies in networkpolicy.yaml, which are what police the database pods One replica, Recreate One cloud websocket; two copies would double every push database.existingSecret: shot-bridge-db-app The bridge reads DATABASE_URL from the Secret CloudNativePG writes for shot-bridge-db (uri key); without it the chart falls back to the SQLite file on the PVC. The PVC stays for the La Marzocco installation key Cluster shot-bridge-db, two instances, 1Gi A few rows a day, but the phones log every shot as it happens; a replica turns a drain or a node loss into a failover of seconds instead of a restart. enablePDB: false still, so the drain triggers that failover rather than hanging, and a topology spread keeps the two on different nodes. WAL and a nightly base backup through backup.yaml HTTPRoute targets the bridge's Service The phone sends Authorization: Bearer; an Authentik outpost in front would answer the app with a login page Probes are TCP /healthz returns 503 whenever the machine is off, and the apps still need the history then apns.env: sandbox The iPhone app is installed from Xcode with development signing; TestFlight builds need production apns.bundleId and apns.teamId Must match the app's bundle ID and team, or APNs rejects every push lm.serial The machine to watch; the chart requires it admin.enabled: true The admin UI's read-only token, and its pods let in on 8080 timeZone: Europe/Zurich The bridge dates a bag's opening by the day of its first shot; the image runs in UTC otherwise, so a shot before 01:00 or 02:00 would land on the day before

items.title: Network policy
items.text:
The chart's CiliumNetworkPolicy selects the bridge's pod; the default-ingress, default-egress and database policies in networkpolicy.yaml select the whole namespace, so the database pods are default-deny too. All at sync wave -2. The shape is Conventions → Ship a CiliumNetworkPolicy.

File Rule Why Chart Ingress on 8080 from ingress and host The Gateway, and the kubelet's probes; the chart admits host alone where the namespace policies below admit remote-node too Chart Ingress on 8080 from the admin UI's pods admin.enabled; the admin UI reads with its token Chart Egress to lion.lamarzocco.io on 443 The La Marzocco REST API and websocket Chart Egress to the Kaffeemacher shop and cdn.shopify.com on 443 The coffee catalog and the bag photos Chart Egress to the four APNs names on 443, 2195 and 2196 Pushes and broadcasts on 443; channel management on 2195 (sandbox) and 2196 (production) Chart Egress to the namespace on database.port The database's -rw Service, rendered because database.existingSecret is set Chart Egress to kube-dns on 53 The chart's own DNS rule; the platform's cluster-wide rule grants the same, so it adds nothing here networkpolicy.yaml Ingress from the namespace, from host and remote-node; egress to the namespace The rules every policy carries, here for the database pods too: What every policy contains; the replica streams from the primary through them networkpolicy.yaml Ingress from Prometheus on 9187, GET /metrics only The database's exporter, through its PodMonitor; the bridge exposes no metrics networkpolicy.yaml Ingress from cnpg-system on 8000 The operator reads the instance manager's status; without it the Cluster never goes Healthy networkpolicy.yaml The instance pods reach kube-apiserver The CloudNativePG instance manager reports its status there; the object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's cnpg-backups policy, see CloudNativePG → Backups

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
Path Keys Written by kv/shot-bridge/accounts lm-username, lm-password, apns-key-id, apns-key-p8 make bao-secrets in the platform repository kv/shot-bridge/config api-key, admin-read-key (the admin UI's read-only token, which it reads from a copy) The PushSecret in secrets.yaml

The accounts path holds values from outside the cluster, so it is its own path: a bao kv put replaces a path wholesale. make bao-secrets asks for the La Marzocco login, then the APNs key ID and the path to the .p8 file; Enter leaves the APNs half empty until the key exists.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
Read the API key and enter it with https://shot.k8s.wlkr.ch in the iPhone app's setup screen; Test shows the machine's state.

kubectl -n shot-bridge get secret shot-bridge -o jsonpath='{.data.BRIDGE_API_KEY}' | base64 -d

items.title: Health check
items.text:
kubectl -n shot-bridge get pods,externalsecret,httproute
curl -s https://shot.k8s.wlkr.ch/healthz    # 200 while the machine is reachable, 503 while it is off
kubectl -n shot-bridge logs deploy/shot-bridge

items.title: Pitfalls
items.text:
• The image and chart have to be public on GHCR. The cluster has no pull secret for ghcr.io/somuch-cloud, and ArgoCD has no credentials for the chart registry.
  • The sync stops at wave -1 until kv/shot-bridge/accounts exists. The ExternalSecret fails on a missing path, so the Deployment is never created; run make bao-secrets.
  • The pod crash-loops while the APNs keys are empty. The bridge exits on a missing variable rather than starting half-configured.
  • Rotating kv/shot-bridge/config changes both keys. The PushSecret writes IfNotExists, so rotating is deleting the path. The phone is logged out: enter the new API key in the app's setup screen, the watch receives it from the phone. The admin UI reads a hand copy of admin-read-key and answers 403 until it is copied again.

items.title: Umami
items.text: Umami counts the visits to every site: the two documentation sites, the GitHub Pages projects and Home Assistant. It sets no cookie and stores no address, so the sites need no consent banner. Upstream publishes an image and no chart, so umami/ is plain manifests around the official image: deployment.yaml, service.yaml, pdb.yaml, httproute.yaml, database.yaml with backup.yaml, secrets.yaml, networkpolicy.yaml and namespace.yaml, per Conventions → Official upstream sources only.

items.title: At a glance
items.text: URL analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch Authentication Authentik proxy outpost, in front of Umami's own login; /script.js and /api/send pass through Storage None outside the database Database CloudNativePG Cluster umami-db Secrets kv/umami/config in OpenBao Files umami/

items.title: Configuration
items.text: Setting Why Plain manifests, no chart One stateless process with one port and one database; the community charts are repackagers The namespace enforces restricted The image runs as uid 1001, needs no capability, and writes only Next.js' cache, which is an emptyDir next to /tmp automountServiceAccountToken: false Umami never talks to the API server DATABASE_URL from umami-db-app, key uri Umami wants one connection string, and CloudNativePG assembles it; see the contract APP_SECRET and TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY from OpenBao The first signs every dashboard session and the second encrypts TOTP secrets; both must survive a rebuild, so the PushSecret writes each to OpenBao once and a rebuilt cluster reads the same value back. See Secrets DISABLE_UPDATES, DISABLE_TELEMETRY, PRIVATE_MODE No phone-home: no version check, no usage report, no favicon fetch for each tracked site. The egress policy allows nothing outside the cluster, so these are what keep the log free of drops Two replicas, a hard spread across nodes, a PodDisruptionBudget Nothing lives on the pod and the sessions are JWTs signed by the shared APP_SECRET, so a second instance keeps the tracker up through a Kured drain and an image bump; the migrations at start take a Postgres advisory lock, so two pods starting together do not race Probes on /api/heartbeat, a long startupProbe The first start runs the Prisma migrations before the server answers revisionHistoryLimit: 2 Superseded ReplicaSets keep their Trivy config-audit reports until garbage collection; the default keeps ten HTTPRoute targets authentik-server, not the app The outpost authenticates and forwards to umami.umami.svc:3000. The provider's skip_path_regex, in the platform repository, exempts exactly /script.js and /api/send: the tracker every visitor loads and the endpoint it posts to. Everything else, the dashboard and the rest of the API, is behind the login. The cross-namespace backendRef works only because the platform's referencegrant.yaml names this namespace; pointing the route at the Umami Service removes the authentication layer, so it deserves a second look in review No CLIENT_IP_HEADER The Gateway's Envoy appends the visitor to X-Forwarded-For and the outpost passes it on; Umami reads that header by default. Only the country is stored, from the bundled GeoLite database, never the address

items.title: Network policy
items.text:
The rules in umami/networkpolicy.yaml, and why each is there. The shape is Conventions → Ship a CiliumNetworkPolicy; rollout and debugging are in Security Policies.

Rule Why Ingress from the namespace, from host and remote-node; egress to the namespace The rules every policy carries: What every policy contains Ingress on 3000 from the Authentik server pods only The outpost proxies the tracker paths as well as the dashboard, so the Gateway never talks to the pod. No fromEntities: ingress, so a request straight from the Gateway cannot skip the login Ingress from Prometheus on 9187, GET /metrics only The database's metrics. Umami itself exposes none Ingress from cnpg-system on 8000 The operator polls the instance manager there; without the rule the Cluster never goes Healthy and the sync deadlocks. See Sync stuck on the database Egress to the namespace only The database. With the three phone-home switches off, nothing else is dialled Egress from the database pod to kube-apiserver The instance manager reports its status there; its liveness check fails otherwise. The object store for WAL and base backups is the platform's cnpg-backups policy, see CloudNativePG → Backups

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
kv/umami/config holds two values, 64 hex characters each as Umami documents them, written once by the PushSecret in secrets.yaml and never overwritten — see Generated secrets.

Key Read as app-secret APP_SECRET: signs the dashboard sessions two-factor-encryption-key TWO_FACTOR_ENCRYPTION_KEY: encrypts TOTP secrets at rest

The ExternalSecret sits at sync wave -1, with the database and ahead of the Deployment that reads it, and keeps its Secret when deleted (deletionPolicy: Retain). The database password is not here; CloudNativePG generates it and nothing outside the cluster needs it.

items.title: First login
items.text: Umami creates admin with the password umami on its first start. Change it under Profile before adding a website; it is the only account, and the only credential Umami keeps that OpenBao does not.

items.title: Adding a site
items.text:
1. Settings → Websites → Add website: a name and the hostname. The website ID it shows is not a secret; it goes into Git with the snippet.

  2. Put the snippet in the site's <head>, with data-domains set to the hostname it should report from:

    <script defer src="https://analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch/script.js"
  data-website-id="<id>" data-domains="<hostname>"></script>

data-domains is what keeps a local zensical serve or npm run dev out of the numbers: the tracker checks the page's hostname before it sends anything. A PR preview under the production hostname is not excluded and counts as a page there.

Where the snippet lives per site:

Site Where This site and the platform documentation overrides/partials/integrations/analytics/custom.html, wired by [project.extra.analytics] provider = "custom" in zensical.toml A SvelteKit or Vite site on GitHub Pages src/app.html or index.html Home Assistant frontend.extra_module_url in configuration.yaml, pointing at a module in the ConfigMap that appends the <script> tag; a module is loaded through import(), which is not how the tracker expects to be run

items.title: Health check
items.text:
kubectl -n umami get pods
kubectl -n umami get cluster umami-db
curl -sI https://analytics.k8s.wlkr.ch/script.js | head -1

The database should report Cluster in healthy state and the script should answer 200 without a redirect to auth.k8s.wlkr.ch. The dashboard's Realtime view is the end-to-end check: open one of the sites and the visit appears within seconds.

items.title: Pitfalls
items.text:
Two logins, and the tracker paths behind neither

Browser users authenticate twice, and /script.js and /api/send are behind neither login; the collect endpoint accepts nothing but page views and events for a known website ID. See Authentik → Pitfalls.

  • A visit shows the cluster's country, or none. Umami takes the visitor from X-Forwarded-For. If every visit resolves to the same place, the header is not reaching the pod: see Behind the Gateway.
  • Deleting kv/umami/config logs everyone out. The PushSecret writes both keys anew: a rotated APP_SECRET invalidates every session and a rotated 2FA key every second factor.
  • data-domains is the only guard against noise. A snippet without it reports from every copy of the site: a laptop, a preview, a fork.
